all_candidates.f1_capacity: PASS, MEASURED. Over 656,309 levels: H(n_orders) = 1.7993 bits, H(n_orders | total shares) = 0.9301 bits, so I(n_orders ; shares) = 0.8692 bits. On levels with >=300 shares: H = 2.8272, H|shares = 1.6332, I = 1.1940 bits. The label is not a constant and the input carries close to a bit of it.
all_candidates.f2_dumb_rule: MARGINAL — MEASURED, AND UNCOMFORTABLY STRONG. Always-answer-1 scores 68.08% exact (P(n=1) = 0.6808). floor(shares/100) scores 61.10%; round(shares/100) 60.33%. But the strongest zero-training rule is an empirical Bayes lookup on the aggregate share count alone — no model, one dict — and it scores 75.86% exact over 13,853 distinct share values. On the interesting subset (shares >= 300) the lookup still gets 58.63% against 45.32% for always-1. So a lookup table with no learning takes three quarters of the task, and the headroom for a learned model is ~24 points. That is the same shape as the round-2 census kill.
all_candidates.f5_saturation_risk: WEAK. The residual entropy is real (0.93–1.63 bits) but the input is low-dimensional (a handful of numbers per level), and the Bayes-optimal single-feature lookup already saturates at n≈10^5 levels because there are only 13,853 distinct share values to condition on. Extra capacity has to come from cross-symbol and temporal context, and I have no measurement that it does. I would not bet on a curve still rising at 10^6.

Published miss rates for these hand-written heuristics are around 20-25%, i.e. the dumb rule already gets ~75-80% of branch directions with no training data at all — and it is not a baseline you invent, it is the incumbent shipping in the buyer's toolchain.

all_candidates.f1_capacity: MEASURED AND FATAL. On 4,185,215 real 2006 tests paired to their 2005 prior test, the single most informative thing a decision register could possibly carry - 'did the same tester regime fail this exact vehicle last year?' - has AUC 0.5077. Count of prior defect items: AUC 0.5180. The published artifact is nearly independent of the decision. Best learned model over all features tops out at 0.6966 AUC on a 32.8% base rate.
all_candidates.f2_dumb_rule: MEASURED. A zero-training two-term rule, score = age/10 + mileage/100000, gets AUC 0.6553 on 400,000 held-out tests. The learned HistGBM (target-encoded make/model + 200 prior-defect-code indicators) scores 0.5740 at n=1e3, 0.6349 at n=1e4 - BELOW the untrained rule - and only overtakes it somewhere near n=3x10^4. This is the census-allocation eight-line-rule failure, reproduced exactly.
all_candidates.f5_saturation_risk: MEASURED AND FATAL. Tabular only: n=1e3 0.5740, 1e4 0.6349, 1e5 0.6763, 1e6 0.6925, 3.79e6 0.6966. The 1.58 orders of magnitude from 1e5 to 3.8e6 bought +0.0203 AUC. I then ran the steelman - added the vehicle's entire prior defect-code history, the richest representation the register admits - and it bought +0.0004 AUC at n=1e6 (0.6929 vs 0.6925). An independent Q1-2005-only run reproduced the shape (dumb 0.6651; learned 0.6834 at 1e5, 0.7065 at 4.65e6). The curve is flat by 1e5, four orders below target.

WHAT I ACTUALLY MEASURED (all from NASDAQ TotalView-ITCH 5.0, 2019-01-30, first 400 MB of the 4.76 GB file = 31,627,545 messages parsed to 09:45:00 ET; scripts and the book snapshot are at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-raise-v1/5d675fa9-5fc4-501c-b3b3-a76510397d00/scratchpad/itch/):

1. Order-book snapshot at 09:45:00 ET: 1,549,395 live displayed orders across 656,309 (symbol, side, price) levels. Recovering the order-count decomposition of an aggregated level: H(n_orders) = 1.7993 bits, H(n_orders | total shares) = 0.9301 bits, I = 0.8692 bits. On the 253,568 levels with >=300 shares: H = 2.8272, H|shares = 1.6332, I = 1.1940 bits. F1 PASSES. But the dumbest rules are strong: always-answer-1 = 68.08%, floor(shares/100) = 61.10%, and an empirical Bayes LOOKUP on the share count alone — one dict, zero training — = 75.86%. F2 MARGINAL, the round-2 census shape.

2. Hidden (non-displayed) liquidity, 09:30:00-09:45:00 ET: 13,242,796 hidden-executed shares against 72,606,429 displayed = 15.43% of volume. Across the 1,454 symbols trading >=5,000 shares, the hidden fraction runs p10 0.018 / median 0.133 / p90 0.372, mean 0.173, sd 0.150. The dumbest rule — give every symbol the market-wide fraction — scores R^2 = -0.0149. NEGATIVE. Worse than the cross-sectional mean.

That second result matters more than the candidate does. DarkFill passes F1 and F2 decisively, has a perfect G2a (the exchange is structurally forbidden from displaying the order, and I confirmed against the ITCH 5.0 message layout that no message type names hidden interest until it executes), and has a genuinely free, self-renewing, environment-supplied label factory. It then dies anyway: G1 (three free days, ~2x10^4 independent symbol-days, Nasdaq licence not open, IEX terms unretrievable — 301 to iexcloud.io/terms, 403 on iexexchange.io) and G4 (the finance venues, not dblp, hold the prior work: 'Prediction of Hidden Liquidity in the Limit Order Book of GLOBEX Futures', Journal of Trading 2013; Hautsch & Huang 'On the hidden side of liquidity'; Bessembinder et al.; 'Hidden and Displayed Liquidity in Securities Markets with Informed Liquidity Providers' 2012 — dblp returned 0 for all three of my hidden-liquidity queries, which is the round-2 publishing-habits trap exactly).

So the round-1/2 finding needs amending. It is NOT true that F1 and F2 cannot both be satisfied — I measured a case where they both are. What is true is that the candidates which satisfy F1 and F2 die one gate later, and for a reason with structure.

A THIRD LAW, WHICH I WOULD BANK ALONGSIDE L1 AND L2:
L3 — A LABEL FACTORY BUILT ON A DELAYED OR PRIVILEGED REVELATION IS VISIBLE TO EVERYONE THE DELAY APPLIES TO. In Scout A's frame there are exactly two ways both halves of the pair can be public. (i) You simulate the destruction yourself on a public source. Then the asymmetry is your own transform, and the training regime is not the deployment regime — SuppressLine can only train on synthetic suppression in the [11,20] beneficiary band and must transfer to [1,10]; ProfileGhost's labels are, for 647k of its 691k executable functions, a property of ExeBench's input generator rather than of any recorded workload. (ii) The destruction is real and a third party reveals the truth on a schedule. Then the revelation channel is a published, well-known data product, which is precisely why the field already built the tool and why the buyer's incumbent is 'wait' or 'buy the better feed'. OfferCurve made this vivid: crossref returned four direct inverse-optimisation efforts on recovering generator offer curves from market outcomes (MISO 2015/2017, marginal offer price recovery 2023, strategic bidding 2017/2018, merit-order 2026), and market clearing is an LP so L2 applies on top. QueueGhost's buyer just subscribes to MBO. TRACECap's buyer just waits for the enhanced file. THE SAME PROPERTY THAT MAKES THE LABELS FREE AT SCALE IS WHAT MAKES G4 CROWDED AND G5 PATIENT.

Verified kills worth keeping regardless of the verdict:
- ExeBench licence is verbatim the round-2 Assemblage kill: 'All C functions keep the original license as per their original Github repository.' And its executable subset is 691,135 functions, BELOW 10^6 — the 4.5M in the abstract counts compilable, not runnable.
- CMS Medicare Provider-and-Service is public domain (data.json license = https://www.usa.gov/government-works) and has ~10^7 provider-years, but I pulled live rows and there is no suppression flag at all: suppressed rows are absent, and the by-Provider Tot_Benes is a distinct-beneficiary count that gives no arithmetic constraint. There is no manufacturer, only a synthetic proxy.
- Backmapping is not a candidate, it is a crowd: 8 direct dblp papers 2023-2026 with released models (FlowBack, HEroBM, CGBack, GenZProt, MSBack, ART-SM), 89 EuropePMC hits. Useful as proof that 'lossy, non-invertible, free labels' is necessary and nowhere near sufficient.
- Audio codec/bitrate recovery from decoded PCM, which looked like a clean physics-destroys-information case, is dead on F4 before F2: crossref returns 'Audio codec identification from coded and transcoded audios' (2013), 'COdec Recognition From Decoded Audio' (2014) and 'Audio Codec Identification with Various Encoding Configurations Using Neural Networks' (2026).
- No open limit-order-book dataset exists at target scale: HuggingFace api/datasets?search='limit order book' returned zero results.

ONE BRANCH I CLOSED FOR A NON-GATE REASON, recorded so nobody re-opens it: the de-identification inverses. The obvious Scout-A shape — recover precise locations from statutorily generalised sensitive-species records (GBIF publishes 3+ billion CC0/CC-BY occurrences, with the same specimen sometimes published precise by the institution and generalised by an aggregator, which is a genuine free label factory) — is an attack tool whose entire purpose is defeating a protection that exists to stop people locating endangered species and sensitive sites. Same for redaction-span prediction on staged declassification releases. I did not develop these, and I would not.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, so it is not credited: I measured F1 and F2 on the two ITCH candidates but measured no learning curve anywhere, so every F5 reading in this submission is an argument rather than a result. I did not read the ERCOT, FINRA or IEX terms. And I would rather report six candidates I actually attacked than pad to ten — the two extra slots past six here (SketchGhost, TRACECap) are thin, and I say so in their own fields.

Nothing in this structure threads the bind, and this round I can say WHY with a measurement rather than an intuition.

THE MEASUREMENT. I built the archetype of Scout B's own brief — "a SEARCH whose result is kept but whose trajectory is discarded" — as six CDCL SAT solvers (CaDiCaL 1.5.3, Glucose 4.2, Lingeling, MiniSat 2.2, MapleChrono, MergeSat 3) on random 3-SAT at n=120, m=492, and ran it on this box. Four numbers:
  (1) Determinism: re-running a solver on the same CNF returned the byte-identical model 1530/1530 = 100.00%.
  (2) Divergence: 0/339 instances had all six solvers agree; pairwise-identical rates were 0–9 of 339. So the artifact genuinely varies with the label — F1 is not the killer.
  (3) ZERO-TRAINING DECODER: "re-run all six solvers and see whose model matches" scores 0.9863 over 1,530 items, 6 classes, chance 0.1667, with only 2.55% ties.
  (4) LEARNED MODEL on 27 joint CNF-x-assignment features, held out by instance group: 0.1920 at 300 rows, 0.2031 at 900, 0.2122 at 3,000, 0.2384 at 13,500. That is +2.8 accuracy points per decade, from a 19% floor, against a free rule at 98.63%. Closing the gap at that slope needs ~27 more decades.
Scripts and data: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-raise-v1/5d675fa9-5fc4-501c-b3b3-a76510397d00/scratchpad/{sat_probe.py,rerun.py,sat_full.py,sat_learn.py,sat_data.json}.

THE LAW IT YIELDS (propose as L3, the sharpened form of L2). Let O = G_s(x): output, generator with setting s, input x. L2 said "if the generator is analytically invertible, a closed-form inverse takes the label." The SAT measurement shows inversion was never required. What is required is only that the generator be RE-RUNNABLE:

  L3. If the generator's INPUT is present in, or is a simple function of, the student's input, and the generator is executable, then re-run-and-compare is a zero-training decoder that takes the whole label. Destroying the trajectory buys nothing, because the trajectory is not needed to reproduce the output.

L3 is strictly stronger than L2 and it is retroactive: it explains AlignerPrint, CallerPrint, AssemblyProv and RefinePrint-PDB from round 2 in one sentence each, and it kills four of my eight candidates a priori — CodonPrint (protein = translate(DNA)), EngineStylo (the position is in the move list), GeomTheory (the molecular graph is read off the coordinates), SolverPrint itself.

WHY THIS IS FATAL TO SCOUT B SPECIFICALLY, NOT JUST TO MY EIGHT. Every shape in my brief — a search whose trajectory is discarded, a heuristic with tie-breaking, a many-to-one aggregation, a composed pipeline, a stochastic process whose seed is discarded, repeated requantisation — names a MACHINE generator. A machine generator is re-runnable by construction. So Scout B's shapes survive L3 only in the sub-case where the generator's input x is itself destroyed. And in that sub-case the trilemma closes:
  (a) x recoverable  -> re-run decoder, MEASURED 0.9863. Dead by A2/L3.
  (b) x destroyed, and s leaves an ARTEFACT SIGNATURE (a lattice, a block grid, a dictionary, a free-list) -> a fixed statistic reads s off. Dead by F2, with the round-1 precedents: byte-histogram nearest centroid 93.91% over 11 classes with no training loop, and the eight-line census rule at AUC 0.8297 beating the learned model everywhere below n=30,000.
  (c) x destroyed, and s leaves no trace separable from the unknown x -> the label is not a function of the input. Dead by F1, with the precedents javac 345/345 byte-identical, ELF base H=0.1518 bits, SPAdes balanced accuracy 0.503.
Only two of my eight candidates reach branch (b)/(c) at all — PresetPrint and SquashSplit — and each dies at a different gate: PresetPrint on G6 (x264 placebo at ~0.3 fps makes a 1e6 preset-labelled corpus months of 4-core wall time, and open UGC source clips number 1e3–1e5, one to three orders under the effective-N target), SquashSplit on G3 (human-legible source code, and "group these edits by intent" is what a frontier model does from a plain prompt) plus a measured G4 of at least five untangling efforts (dblp 2015 x2, 2017; Crossref 2018 program slicing, 2022 attributed graph clustering, 2025 composite-commit detection).

WHY VPT IS NOT A COUNTEREXAMPLE, AND WHERE THE REMAINING SPACE IS. VPT survives L3 because its generator is a HUMAN, and a human is not re-runnable: you cannot replay the player on the same frame and read off the keypress. The non-re-runnable generators are the ones with a person or the physical world in the loop, which is Scout A's and Scout C's territory, not mine. My honest read is that Scout B's brief, as written, selects for exactly the property that makes the label free — and that this is a structural result about the search space, not a failure of effort on these eight. I would rather this round record that finding than have me nominate PresetPrint or SquashSplit and let an adversarial review discover the same thing at greater cost. I am not putting anything forward for SELECT.

Nothing in this structure threads the bind, and I think I can now say WHY rather than just reporting another zero.

WHAT I MEASURED. I took the largest, cleanest, most open decision register I could find anywhere in Scout C's territory - the UK MOT test archive, OGL v3, ~500M recorded tester decisions, ~38M independent vehicles, no effective-N problem, no licence problem, no frontier-model problem, no crowding problem - and measured it end to end. I downloaded test_result_2005 (7,499,745 rows), test_result_2006 (2.78 GB raw) and test_item_2005 (9,844,490 defect rows over 1,629 RfR codes), paired 4,185,215 real 2006 tests to their 2005 prior test, and held out 400,000.

  Zero-training rule, score = age/10 + mileage/100000 .......... AUC 0.6553
  Learned HistGBM, n=1e3 / 1e4 / 1e5 / 1e6 / 3.79e6 ............ 0.5740 / 0.6349 / 0.6763 / 0.6925 / 0.6966
  Same, plus 200 prior-defect-code indicators .................. 0.5729 / 0.6371 / 0.6767 / 0.6929
  "Did it fail last year?" ..................................... AUC 0.5077
  "How many defects last year?" ................................ AUC 0.5180

Three things follow. (1) F2: the untrained two-term rule beats the learned model at every n below about 3x10^4. (2) F5: the 1.58 orders of magnitude from 1e5 to 3.8e6 bought +0.0203 AUC, and the whole prior-defect-code history - the entire richness the register contains - bought +0.0004. (3) The killer, F1: the tester's OWN PREVIOUS DECISION on the SAME VEHICLE predicts the next decision at AUC 0.5077. The channel from the published artifact to the recorded judgement is very nearly closed.

THE LAW THIS SUGGESTS, offered for the record alongside L1 and L2:

  L3. A DECISION REGISTER PUBLISHES THE DECISION, NOT THE STATE. Registers exist for accountability,
      not prediction. What they publish is a short coded row chosen so the decision can be audited and
      counted - twenty to forty fields. That row's channel capacity is fixed and small, so the learning
      curve flattens two to four orders of magnitude below 1e6 and a hand-written rule takes most of what
      is there. Where the high-dimensional state at decision time IS public, the decision labels are on
      the far side of a licence wall (eBird's terms forbid redistribution outright; OPTN needs a DUA;
      Network Rail's attribution moved to a registration-gated marketplace and the TRUST movement archive
      that would be the input has no open bulk release at all) or the field has already built and deployed
      the model (Lichess runs Irwin and Kaladin on the CC0 games; the FAA runs configuration prediction in
      TFDM; MIT published four papers on runway-configuration choice).

That is the same tension the brief describes, but sharpened: in Scout C's territory the asymmetry is not merely large, it is TOTAL. The MOT tester put the car on a ramp. The fire officer stood in the burned room. The delay-attribution clerk read the signaller's log. In every case the private information is the whole of the evidence and the public artifact is an identifier plus a date. VPT worked because consecutive video frames retain statistical evidence of the action; a registration document retains almost no statistical evidence of what a mechanic decided about a set of brake pads.

ONE CANDIDATE I COULD NOT KILL AND COULD NOT CLEAR: UK rail delay attribution. It is the only one whose artifact is genuinely high-dimensional (a graph of hundreds of trains' timings over an area and period), whose asymmetry is real without being total, whose label is a 250-way code no published rule derives from timings, and whose buyer pays nine figures a year for exactly this. I could not test it because both halves are behind walls - the labels moved to the Rail Data Marketplace and the movement-data inputs have no open historical archive. I recorded the full field list (extracted from Network Rail's own explanation PDF) so a future round can pick it up if the licence position changes, and I flagged the two fields - Responsible Manager and Incident number - that would make the study circular if left in. But UNVERIFIED is not PASS, and G1 as written demands a named licence with a URL. It does not have one.

My read: SELECT nothing. The prereg's NO VIABLE DOMAIN FOUND is the correct terminal verdict for this scout, and the MOT numbers above are the strongest single piece of evidence for it that Phase 0 has produced from this direction - a candidate that passed G1, G3, G6 and G4 cleanly and still died at F1/F2/F5 on measurement.

NO VIABLE DOMAIN FOUND. This pool contains nothing real, and I am not returning a survivor to avoid the prereg's terminal verdict.

THE DECISIVE TABULATION. The prereg requires G2a/G3/G1/G6/G4 all at PASS. Not one of the 26 candidates achieves that, and it is not close — every candidate fails at least one gate outright, most fail two or three. The two candidates with a clean, verified, redistributable G1 are precisely the two the scouts measured hardest, and both died on measurement rather than argument: MOT (OGL v3, ~38M vehicles, G3/G4/G6 all passing) died at F1 with the same vehicle's own prior outcome predicting the next at AUC 0.5077, at F2 against an untrained two-term rule at 0.6553, and at F5 with 1.58 orders of magnitude buying +0.0203 AUC; SuppressLine (US public domain, 1e7 provider-years) died at G2 because pulling live rows showed suppressed lines are simply absent with no flag and no arithmetic constraint, so there is no manufacturer to build at all.

WHAT I VERIFIED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED. I re-attacked the only candidate with a measured F1 AND F2 pass, because a wrong kill there would have changed the verdict. DarkFill's G2a is flawless and its F2 result is the best in Phase 0 (the market-wide-constant rule scores R^2 = -0.0149, negative). It dies anyway, and I confirmed the kill from a second direction: Crossref returns 'CME iceberg order detection and prediction' (Quantitative Finance 2020) — the prediction task itself, in a top field venue — alongside four more direct efforts. G4 FAIL, verified. I also corrected the record in the candidate's favour where the scout was wrong: there are 15 free Nasdaq ITCH sample days, not 3, raising effective N to ~1.3e5 symbol-days. It does not save it — still 0.9 orders below target, still not redistributable. And I recorded one kill I could NOT sustain: PresetPrint's G4 is not crowded (three Crossref formulations plus arXiv returned only adjacent double-compression and GOP-estimation work), so a future round must kill it on G1/G6, which it does decisively, rather than on a G4 it does not have.

THE STRUCTURAL FINDING, WHICH IS THE REAL OUTPUT OF THIS ROUND. Three scouts working independently each derived a law and each numbered it L3, and the three are the same law seen from three sides. Unify them: for a label to be free at scale, the labelling must ALREADY be someone's job or someone's by-product — and there are exactly three ways that happens, each destroying a different gate. (i) A MACHINE does it, so the machine is re-runnable and re-run-and-compare is a zero-training decoder — MEASURED at 0.9863 over six SAT solvers, with the learned model at 0.2384 rising +2.8 points per decade. (ii) An INSTITUTION reveals it on a schedule, so the revelation channel is a well-known published product, which is exactly why the field already built the tool and why the buyer's incumbent is 'wait' or 'buy the better feed' — measured as four direct efforts on hidden liquidity and four on offer-curve inverse optimisation. (iii) A HUMAN records it in a register, and a register publishes the DECISION, not the STATE — twenty to forty audited fields whose channel capacity is fixed and small — MEASURED at AUC 0.5077 for the strongest feature a register could possibly carry.

WHY VPT ESCAPES AND NOTHING HERE DOES. VPT is a fourth case this pool contains zero instances of: the label is a by-product of a human acting on a rich sensor stream, where the stream itself is the published artifact. Case (iii) fails precisely because a register row is a DESCRIPTION of a decision, whereas a video frame is a physical EFFECT of one, at 20 Hz across two million pixels. The missing generator class is a HIGH-BANDWIDTH PHYSICAL RECORDING THAT IS THE CAUSAL CONSEQUENCE OF THE HIDDEN VARIABLE, published in bulk for a reason unrelated to the label. Twenty-six candidates, and not one has it. The nearest miss is Lichess ToS marks — genuinely rich sequences with real F5 headroom — and it dies because the buyer already runs the learned version in production, plus the labels are not in the CC0 dump and shipping them would mean redistributing a list of named individuals accused of cheating.

Across three rounds: 99 candidates, 11 adversarial reviews, 0 SELECT. The gates did not fail to find a domain; they correctly identified that the search space as framed — machine generators, scheduled revelations, and decision registers — is exhausted, and that the one class that would work was never in it. I record NO VIABLE DOMAIN FOUND as the finding, not the failure.

rejected.name: DarkFill — predicting non-displayed (hidden) liquidity from the displayed book
rejected.reason: The strongest candidate in Phase 0 and the only one with a measured F1 AND F2 pass (per-symbol hidden fraction sd 0.150 on mean 0.173; the market-wide-constant rule scores R^2 = -0.0149, NEGATIVE). G2a is flawless — verified against the ITCH 5.0 layout, no message type names hidden interest until it executes. It still dies twice. G4: I re-ran the crowding check from a second direction and Crossref returns 'CME iceberg order detection and prediction' (Quantitative Finance 2020) — the prediction task itself in a top field venue — plus 'The Impact of Iceberg Orders in Limit Order Books' (2009), 'Hidden and Displayed Liquidity in Securities Markets with Informed Liquidity Providers' (RFS 2013), 'Liquidity Estimation: Lit and Dark Liquidity with Lost Time Data' (2014), 'Accessing Displayed and Non-Displayed Liquidity' (J. Trading 2006). That is >=4 direct efforts, far past the <3 bar, and it is the round-2 publishing-habits trap exactly (dblp returned 0). G1: I corrected the scout's count — the Nasdaq emi directory lists 15 free sample days, not 3 — but 15 days x ~8,700 symbols is ~1.3e5 independent symbol-days, still 0.9 orders below target, and the Nasdaq Global Data Agreement makes the artifact non-shippable for Phase 3.

rejected.name: QueueGhost — order-count decomposition of an aggregated depth level
rejected.reason: F2 measured and uncomfortably strong: an empirical Bayes lookup on the aggregate share count alone — one dict, zero training — scores 75.86% exact, leaving ~24 points of headroom. That is the round-2 census shape. G5 is fatal and clean: the buyer's incumbent is not a free tool but a purchase — subscribe to the MBO feed and read the answer exactly. G2a also leaks in the spec, since CME MDP 3.0 MBP-10 carries NumberOfOrders (FIX tag 346). G1 same licence and effective-N failure as DarkFill.

rejected.name: OfferCurve-60Day — confidential generator offer curves from public market outcomes
rejected.reason: Market clearing is a linear program and recovering objective coefficients from an LP solution is inverse optimisation — a tractable convex programme. L2 fires at cut 1. G2a also leaks arithmetically: the LMP at a node IS the marginal resource's offer price at its cleared quantity, so the label is printed in the input for exactly the resource everyone cares about. G4 independently crowded (four direct inverse-optimisation efforts). F2 likely fatal: offer = heat rate x gas price + VOM is the industry's own two-parameter formula.

rejected.name: ProfileGhost — executed branch/basic-block profile from compiled code
rejected.reason: ExeBench's card is verbatim the round-2 Assemblage kill: 'All C functions keep the original license as per their original Github repository.' Not shippable. Count is 691,135 executable functions, BELOW 1e6 — the 4.5M in the abstract counts compilable, not runnable. F3: the asymmetry is FAKE for 94% of the corpus, since with machine-synthesised I/O the 'recorded execution' is a property of ExeBench's input generator rather than any real workload. F2: LLVM's BranchProbabilityInfo (Ball-Larus/Wu-Larus heuristics) already ships in the buyer's toolchain at ~75-80% with zero training data. G6 also fails — compiling and running 1e6 functions is many CPU-days on 4 cores.

rejected.name: SuppressLine — reconstructing suppressed small-cell rows in Medicare data
rejected.reason: The most interesting kill in the pool because G1 genuinely PASSES — data.json license is https://www.usa.gov/government-works, public domain, ~1e7 provider-years. The scout pulled live rows rather than trusting docs and found there is NO suppression flag: suppressed rows are simply ABSENT, and the by-Provider Tot_Benes is a distinct-beneficiary count giving no arithmetic constraint. So the student cannot even know which HCPCS codes are missing. There is no label factory, only synthetic re-suppression in the [11,20] band that must transfer to [1,10] — a guaranteed shift across exactly the boundary that matters. Label is <=3.32 bits over a low-dimensional tabular row; F5 is the census shape.

rejected.name: BackMap — atomistic coordinates from a coarse-grained configuration
rejected.reason: Passes L2 cleanly — a bead centroid is consistent with a continuum of atomistic configurations, genuinely lossy and non-invertible. Dies at G4 with counts: 8 direct dblp backmapping papers 2023-2026 (FlowBack, HEroBM, CGBack, GenZProt, MSBack, ART-SM among them), several with released pre-trained models, 89 EuropePMC hits. Worth banking as the cleanest proof that the target property is NECESSARY BUT NOWHERE NEAR SUFFICIENT.

rejected.name: SketchGhost — multiset structure from a fixed-size streaming sketch
rejected.reason: The field built the analytic inverse BEFORE it built the sketch: HLL ships a closed-form cardinality estimator with bias correction, Count-Min a closed-form frequency bound, and MLE entropy estimators for sketches exist. The dumb rule is the estimator in the library, with a proven error bound. Beating a provably near-optimal estimator is a losing framing. Corpus is also self-generated, so the asymmetry is over your own stream generator rather than the world.

rejected.name: TRACECap — true size of size-capped corporate bond trades
rejected.reason: The label is a one-dimensional conditional-tail expectation above a known threshold — fit a Pareto tail and report the conditional mean, ten lines, no learning. That is L1 in its purest form, the same object the Sentinel-1 poly5+2cpr fit disposed of. Enhanced Historical is a paid FINRA product with subscriber terms. The scout explicitly flagged this one as unscreened rather than screened-and-passed; the leak check was never performed.

rejected.name: SolverPrint — CDCL solver identity from a satisfying assignment
rejected.reason: The decisive measurement of the round. Re-running each solver on the same CNF reproduced the byte-identical model 1530/1530 = 100.00%. The zero-training decoder 're-run all six and see whose model matches' scores 0.9863 over 1,530 items at 6 classes; the learned model on 27 features reaches 0.2384 at 13,500 rows, rising +2.8 points per decade — ~27 more decades to close the gap. Discarding the trajectory bought nothing because the trajectory was never needed: the generator's input (the CNF) is in the student's input.

rejected.name: PresetPrint — encoder preset and rate-control mode from decoded pixels
rejected.reason: Genuinely survives L2 and L3 — the source video is destroyed so the encoder cannot be re-run — which makes it the structurally cleanest candidate against the laws. It dies on the hard gates instead. G1: the independent unit is the pristine source clip, and open UGC corpora hold 1e3-1e5 of them, one to three orders below target; a 1e6-clip pristine corpus does not exist openly at any licence. G6: 1e6 frames of 1080p YUV is 3.1 TB against a 30 GB disk, and even at 64x64 blocks the ENCODE cost dominates — x264 placebo at ~0.3 fps makes 1e5 clips x 10 presets months of 4-core wall time. NOTE FOR THE RECORD: I could NOT sustain a G4 kill here. Three Crossref formulations and an arXiv query returned no direct preset-attribution effort, only adjacent double-compression and GOP-size-estimation work. A future round should not kill this on a G4 it does not have — F2 (partition-size histogram, the ISA shape) is the untested risk.

rejected.name: BtreeHistory — insertion/deletion history from a SQLite B-tree page
rejected.reason: rowid is monotonic in insertion order by default and stored in the cell, so sorting by rowid recovers the insertion permutation with essentially zero error and zero training; parsing the free-block list recovers deletion evidence deterministically. These are not hypothetical rules, they are the shipping tools (bring2lite, SPaRe, undark). The lossy part and the informative part barely overlap. Corpus is also 100% synthetic, so there is no abundant unlabelled corpus in the FDM-1 sense.

rejected.name: CodonPrint — codon-optimisation tool from a synthetic coding sequence
rejected.reason: protein = translate(DNA) is a one-line function of the student's own input, so the optimiser is re-runnable: run every tool on the translated protein and compare, exactly the 0.9863 precedent. Even without re-running, CAI against each host table plus GC3 is a ~20-line nearest-centroid rule of the shape that scored 93.91% on the ISA task. G3 also rising fast against genome foundation models.

rejected.name: SquashSplit — commit partition from a squashed union diff
rejected.reason: The input is human-legible source code and the task is literally 'group these edits by intent' — the single thing G3 names as auto-fail, and a frontier model does it from a plain prompt today, already shipped inside Copilot. Independently G4 measures at >=5 untangling efforts (dblp 2015 x2, 2017; Crossref 2018 slicing, 2022 attributed graph clustering, 2025 composite-commit detection), and diffs are derivative works needing a permissive-only subset (the Assemblage problem).

rejected.name: EngineStylo — chess engine identity from a move sequence
rejected.reason: The board position is fully present in the move sequence, so every candidate engine is re-run on every position and its move compared — which is precisely how fair-play adjudication is done today. G5: the buyer already holds Regan's IPR model plus Lichess's Irwin and Kaladin, free and deployed.

rejected.name: RollupInverse — raw-distribution structure from a quantile sketch
rejected.reason: Standard interpolation within the digest is the field's own estimator and is what the sketch was engineered to make accurate; the learned model competes against a design guarantee. The residual is a parameter fit with a small bias correction — L1 exactly, the Sentinel-1 shape. The digest is a near-sufficient statistic for what it preserves and near-uninformative about what it discarded, so F1 is weak by construction.

rejected.name: GeomTheory — level of theory from an optimised molecular geometry
rejected.reason: The molecular graph is read off the coordinates by bond perception and the graph is the generator's input, so re-optimising at each candidate level reproduces the geometry to numerical precision. Expensive is not the same as impossible, and A2 asks whether a deterministic decoder exists, not whether it is cheap. F2: a lookup of mean C-C/C-N/C-O bond length per functional is ~15 lines, the census shape. Differences live in the third decimal — per-bond-type means converge in the thousands.

rejected.name: DVSA MOT tester pass/fail and itemised-defect decision
rejected.reason: The single most valuable negative result Phase 0 produced, because G1 (OGL v3, verified via CKAN, ~38M vehicles, no effective-N problem), G3, G4 and G6 all PASS cleanly and it still dies. F1 is the killer: the same vehicle's OWN PREVIOUS test outcome predicts the next decision at AUC 0.5077, and prior defect count at 0.5180 — the channel from artifact to judgement is nearly closed. F2: a zero-training two-term rule (age/10 + mileage/100000) scores 0.6553, beating the learned model at every n below ~3e4. F5: 1e5 -> 3.79e6 bought +0.0203 AUC, and the entire prior-defect-code history bought +0.0004. Reproduced on an independent Q1-2005 split.

rejected.name: UK rail delay attribution — DAG cause code
rejected.reason: The 'could not kill, could not clear' candidate, and it stays uncleared. G1 as written demands a named licence with a URL; there is none — no historic delay-attribution package on data.gov.uk (81 hits searched), the labels moved to the registration-gated Rail Data Marketplace, and the INPUT side (historical TRUST/Darwin movement archives) has no open bulk release at all, so BOTH halves are behind walls. UNVERIFIED is not PASS. G6 independently fails: a per-incident network-state context window is 1e4-1e5 bytes/unit, i.e. 10-100 GB at the 1M rung against a 30 GB disk. G2a also carries the census-codebook leak in duplicate — Responsible Manager is co-determined with the cause code, and Incident number silently groups all records sharing one label.

rejected.name: eBird regional reviewer approve/reject on flagged checklists
rejected.reason: The terms forbid redistributing eBird data and forbid passing it to another user; each user must request access themselves. Same class as the round-2 KiK-net and INTERMAGNET kills. Independently F3: the reviewer's primary evidence IS the checklist the student sees, so most of the task is distillation — the crystallography pattern — and the flag itself was produced by a regional-filter threshold rule, so a no-training rarity threshold takes the majority.

rejected.name: NFIRS fire-officer Cause of Ignition determination
rejected.reason: Fails on the codebook. NFIRS enforces relational edit rules validating Heat Source, Item First Ignited and especially Factor Contributing To Ignition AGAINST Cause Of Ignition, all filled by the same officer in the same sitting. Those must be deleted — and deleting them is precisely what collapsed the census candidate from 0.9082 to 0.6821. Everything informative sits on the wrong side of the leak; what survives is property use, hour and area of origin, which a five-line vacancy-plus-hour rule takes. NFIRS is also voluntary and non-census, which USFA warns about explicitly.

rejected.name: OPTN organ-offer accept/decline decision
rejected.reason: STAR files require a signed DUA with UNOS/SRTR and redistribution is prohibited. Independently the effective-N failure is the round-2 3,271,826-rows/122,550-groups shape in a new costume: one donor generates hundreds of correlated offer rows sharing one organ, so the independent unit is donors at ~1.5e4/year, ~5e5 over three decades — below target on its own. F2: 'decline if KDPI > 85' plus centre base rate takes most of it, and the offer-acceptance ML literature is already substantial.

rejected.name: Airport runway configuration selection
rejected.reason: 'Keep the current configuration' is a one-line rule with no training and on quarter-hourly data is correct the overwhelming majority of the time; headwind alignment handles most of the rest. The incumbent configuration is legitimately available at decision time, which makes the task mostly a persistence problem rather than a learning problem. G4: FAA/NASA already field configuration prediction inside TFDM and ATD-2, and MIT published four papers on it. Effective N on the idiosyncratic-decider axis is 77 airports.

rejected.name: Lichess moderator terms-of-service marks
rejected.reason: The learned version already exists and is in production AT THE BUYER: Lichess runs Irwin and Kaladin, deployed neural cheat detectors, on exactly this data. G1 is split and failing — the games are CC0 but the marks are NOT in the dump, existing only as a per-user API field, so building the label set means mass-scraping millions of profiles and then redistributing a list of named individuals accused of cheating. Not shippable on licence or on ethics. G6 also fails at ~200 KB/account, ~200 GB at the 1M rung. Notable as the one candidate whose artifact has genuine F5 headroom — and it is killed by everything else.

rejected.name: HMDA mortgage underwriting decision and denial reasons
rejected.reason: This is the single most-modelled tabular decision register in existence — CFPB, the Urban Institute and every bank's compliance vendor run HMDA models; G4 fails by orders of magnitude, not by a margin. F2: a threshold on DTI alone, or logistic regression on DTI/CLTV/LTI, takes the large majority. Effective N is also compromised — the deciders are ~4,000 institutions and the top lenders each decide millions of times, so one institution deciding 500,000 times is not 500,000 draws. ~25 coded features guarantees the MOT saturation shape.

rejected.name: X.509 revocation reason code
rejected.reason: Revocations are dominated by bulk incidents, so 'majority reason code for this issuer on this issuance day' is a pure lookup with no training that would plausibly take 80-90% — the ISA-histogram shape. Effective N is the incident count (~1e3-1e4) because one decision covers 1e5+ certificates at once, a severe failure. And G5 has no credible buyer at all: the operationally useful fact is THAT a certificate was revoked, which crt.sh and the CCADB dashboards already give away free.

rejected.name: SIMBAD curator object-type assignment
rejected.reason: Photometric source classification is one of the most crowded ML tasks in astronomy, with dozens of released models, public benchmarks, and LSST shipping its own classifier. F2: colour-colour cuts have separated stars, galaxies and quasars for forty years with no training at accuracies in the 90s for the dominant classes. G2a also leaks — the identifier prefix and bibliographic reference count encode which survey found the object, which is nearly the label for many classes.
